stories.headline: Magnitude 4.5 Earthquake strikes Assam's Nagaon
stories.title: Magnitude 4.5 Earthquake strikes Assam's Nagaon
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Assam's Nagaon district witnessed a 4.5 -magnitude earthquake at the wee hours of 4:23 am on Tuesday, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS).
The seismic waves originated at a depth of 33 km, with the epicenter recorded at 26.428 degree North and 93.060 degree East latitude.

The National Centre for Seismology provided these details on X: “EQ of M: 4.5, On: 06/10/2026 04:23:47 IST, Lat: 26.428 N, Long: 93.060 E, Depth: 33 Km, Location: Nagaon, Assam.” They also posted a link to their app, BhooKamp, for more information.
No casualties reported till now.

stories.headline: CEC & Election Commissioners Enjoy Greater Legal Immunity Than Even Judges, Remarks Supreme Court
stories.title: CEC & Election Commissioners Enjoy Greater Legal Immunity Than Even Judges, Remarks Supreme Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (October 5) orally observed that the legal protection granted to the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners under the 2023 law may be broader than the protection available even to constitutional court judges, during the hearing of petitions challenging the decisions allegedly taken unilaterally by CEC Gyanesh Kumar in connection with the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing the petitions.

Senior Advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the petitioner, argued that the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners(Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, had substantially enhanced the authority and immunity of the CEC and Election Commissioners.
As per Section 16 of the 2023 Act, CEC and Election Commissioners are protected from civil or criminal proceedings for acts done in the discharge or purported discharge of their official functions.
The legal protection continues even after they have demitted office.
At this stage, Justice Bagchi made a significant observation regarding the extent of the protection.
"This protection is perhaps only for the President.
It does not apply even to judges," Justice Bagchi observed.
Singh agreed with the observation and argued that the statutory scheme had placed the CEC in a position of extraordinary legal protection.
"Even the Prime Minister does not have this," Singh submitted.
He argued that the statutory framework had effectively placed the CEC "on a pedestal even higher than Supreme Court judges."
"ECI more powerful today than any other constitutional authority," Singh submitted.

“He said this is an open court...

The CJI clearly said that we do not approve Form 6.

stories.headline: INDIA bloc MPs begin march to EC demanding CEC's resignation; security tightened
stories.title: INDIA bloc MPs begin march to EC demanding CEC's resignation; security tightened
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 06: MPs of the INDIA bloc began a march from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters on Tuesday to demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation amid allegations of irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls. Leaders of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi was among the leaders taking part in the march. The march began amid heavy security deployment and barricading in and around Parliament and the Election Commission headquarters. Security personnel were stationed in the area much before the MPs began arriving. Ahead of the march, opposition MPs questioned the security arrangements and stepped up their demand for Kumar's resignation, citing the Supreme Court's observations on changes to Form 6, the statutory application for enrolment as a voter. Congress MP Imran Masood accused Kumar of eroding public trust in the Election Commission. "Across the country, the institution that Gyanesh Kumar headed was an institution the entire country trusted, an institution the entire country took pride in and felt proud of. Questions were never raised over its impartiality. One person has broken that trust," he told PTI Videos. "And an entire nexus is working together. We will question Gyanesh Kumar, and the BJP chief ministers will start giving the answers," he alleged. CPI MP P Sandosh Kumar said the Supreme Court's observations on Monday had strengthened the opposition's objections to the additional declaration attached to Form 6 during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. "On September 26, there was a press statement by the Commission and it was stated that the entire process related to Form 6 has been ratified by the Supreme Court. Whereas it has been proven that it is an entirely misleading statement," he alleged. Calling the CEC a "Cheating Election Commissioner", the CPI leader said opposition parties had been agitating against the provisions since 2025 and would intensify their movement. Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut questioned the scale of security deployment ahead of the march, saying the MPs intended to proceed peacefully. "We are MPs. We are members of Parliament. We are also citizens of this country. Why is there a need to deploy such a large force to stop us? We will walk and go. We are unarmed," he said. Raut claimed that Border Security Force and CISF personnel had been deployed and security outside ministers' residences increased. Accusing Kumar of misleading the public over the Supreme Court's position on Form 6, he said the CEC had "no moral right" to continue in office. The Supreme Court on Monday said it had not approved any modified version of Form 6 and would examine the Election Commission's records to ascertain whether changes had been made and who had authorised them. The observations were made while hearing a petition challenging alleged unilateral decisions by Kumar. In its September 26 statement, the Commission had said the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR had been upheld by the Supreme Court, while forms prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, would be used outside the SIR period. The march comes amid an opposition campaign over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise and reports of differences within the three-member Commission. The poll body has rejected suggestions of a split and maintained that decisions relating to SIR were taken unanimously.

stories.headline: Harmanpreet Kaur steps down from India women's team captaincy
stories.title: Harmanpreet Kaur steps down from India women's team captaincy
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 06: Indian women's cricket team's long-serving captain Harmanpreet Kaur on Tuesday stepped down from her position in all three formats, saying that she has done her duty as leader and is now "ready to play for the love of the game again." Harmanpreet's announcement came after a BCCI review meeting in Guwahati to evaluate the team's trajectory in the past few months. Chaired by BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia, the meeting was attended by Harmanpreet, vice-captain Smriti Mandhana and head coach Amol Muzumdar. The 37-year-old led the Indian T20 side for a decade, taking over the position in 2016, and was elevated to ODI captaincy in 2022 before becoming the all-format leader in 2023. "Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Women's Cricket Team across all formats," she posted on her instagram account. "This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life," Harmanpreet said in a lengthy statement. "Now, I'm ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues," she added. Harmanpreet, under whom India won its maiden ODI World Cup in November last year and recently picked up a second successive Asian Games gold in the T20 format, said she is leaving the captaincy "with a heart full of emotions, but also with peace." "Because I genuinely believe my team is in a good place," she said.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) agreed to urgently hear the Punjab government against a State High Court order directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to register a case and probe allegations of corruption against the office of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.
Appearing before Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, senior advocates Vikas Singh and Shadan Farasat, for the State government, said the order violated the very basic principles of federalism.
Mr. Singh said the State was poll-bound, and a Central agency has been ordered to investigate allegations.
Mr. Singh said the allegations regard administrative matters like transfers, etc, but the High Court has ordered a criminal case to be registered.
“This is a State going to polls soon.
During election time, these kinds of cases are trumped up.
The very federal structure has been violated,” he submitted.
The Chief Justice said the court would endeavour to list the case for hearing in the next 24 hours or definitely hear it on October 8.
The High Court had, on October 5, directed the CBI to probe corruption allegations linked to Chief Minister Mann’s office.

stories.headline: Supreme Court 7-Judge Bench Disposes Reference On Legislative Privilege As Infructuous
stories.title: Supreme Court 7-Judge Bench Disposes Reference On Legislative Privilege As Infructuous
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today closed the 7-judge reference on the issue of legislative privileges vis-a-vis free speech, noting that the 2003 resolution of the Tamil Nadu legislative assembly, which was the trigger for the case, was withdrawn in 2004.

A bench comprising CJI Surya Kant, Justice Aravind Kumar, Justice PK Mishra, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice Vipul Pancholi, Justice Shree Chandrashekhar and Justice V Mohana was constituted to hear the matter, which had been pending for nearly 2 decades.
Today, while disposing of the matter as infructuous, the bench noted that the withdrawal of the impugned resolution skipped the notice of the Court while passing the reference order.
The bench observed that the cause of action for the reference has become infructuous, and closed the matter.
However, the bench left the questions of law open for adjudication in an appropriate case.

stories.headline: Punjab Govt Moves Supreme Court Against HC Order For CBI Probe Into Corruption Allegations Linked To Chief Minister's Office
stories.title: Punjab Govt Moves Supreme Court Against HC Order For CBI Probe Into Corruption Allegations Linked To Chief Minister's Office
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Punjab government has moved the Supreme Court challenging the Punjab and Haryana High Court's order directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to register a criminal case and probe allegations of corruption linked to the office of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.
The Special Leave Petition (SLP) was filed by the State government, challenging the order passed by the High Court on Monday.

A High Court bench comprising Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor had on Monday directed the CBI to register a criminal case into allegations concerning Rajbir Singh Ghuman, Officer on Special Duty (OSD) to Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann.
The High Court further directed the State of Punjab and the Punjab.
Police to provide all assistance to the CBI for conducting a fair investigation.
The directions were passed while hearing a Public Interest Litigation filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf.
The PIL alleged that the Punjab.
Police had failed to take appropriate action despite communications from the Enforcement Directorate (ED) seeking a probe into allegations against Ghuman.

According to the submissions before the High Court, the ED had flagged allegations involving one Nitin Gohal, who allegedly acted as an intermediary for persons seeking various favours from the Punjab government.
The allegations relate, among other things, to facilitating transfers, providing access to confidential government documents, facilitating arms licences and securing other benefits.
The High Court, after considering the material placed before it, directed the CBI to register a criminal case and investigate the allegations.
The Punjab government's challenge before the Supreme Court seeks to overturn the High Court's direction for a CBI investigation.

stories.headline: India’s blind women cricketers still wait for house sites and jobs a year after their World Cup win
stories.title: India’s blind women cricketers still wait for house sites and jobs a year after their World Cup win
stories.summary: Captain Deepika T.C. of Madakasira in Andhra Pradesh’s Sri Sathya Sai district is still waiting for the house site she was promised
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'world cup' in title weight 42
article_sentences: Deepika T.C. captained India to victory in the first Women’s T20 World Cup for the Blind in November 2025.
Nearly a year later, she is still waiting for the house site that leaders and officials promised her.
She and her 15 teammates, who won the tournament hosted jointly by India and Sri Lanka, say they are unable to get the support they need from society and the government in their day-to-day lives.
They do not get playgrounds and fitness guidance in their localities, and they cannot afford training in big cities.
Leaders who make tall promises in public have shown little interest in ensuring government jobs and house sites for them, they said.
Ms. Deepika hails from Madakasira in Sri Sathya Sai district.
“Due to our partial vision issues, we cannot move around government offices to follow up on house site issues.
The government has to do its own and instill confidence among us,” she told.
The Hindu.
Ms. Deepika, who developed vision problems as an infant, completed a degree course and focused on cricket in spite of her family’s financial struggles.
Her parents, Timmappa and Chittemma, encouraged her to practise cricket in Bengaluru although they had many fears about her partial vision.
She has been consistently playing well and won special recognition when she scored 92 runs off 45 balls against Australia in a World Cup match.

stories.headline: 'Tried To Softly Bend Law Towards Justice': Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya Bids Farewell To Delhi High Court
stories.title: 'Tried To Softly Bend Law Towards Justice': Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya Bids Farewell To Delhi High Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
article_sentences: Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya on Tuesday bid farewell to the Delhi High Court on his elevation to the Supreme Court of India, saying that throughout his judicial career, he had tried to “bind law, justice, and compassion together.”

A function was organized by the Delhi High Court today in order to bid farewell to CJ Upadhyaya, which was attended by all the judges as well as Central and Delhi Government counsels as well as lawyers.
On September 28, the Supreme Court Collegium had recommended elevation of Justice Upadhyaya.
Yesterday evening, the Central Government notified his appointment.
In his farewell address, CJ Upadhyaya reflected on his journey from practising as an advocate in Lucknow to serving on the Bench and eventually heading the Delhi High Court.
“Like other judges, I came across unforeseen situations when law was not able to ensure a just outcome in the case, and it appeared isolated from justice.
In such situations, I tried to softly bend the law towards justice for the deserving litigant, and to be able to do so has been a blessing for me,” he said.
Justice Upadhyaya, however, added that he could not himself determine whether he had succeeded in imparting justice.
“I cannot tell whether or not I have succeeded in imparting justice.
In fact, I should not even try because it would be an act of deciding my own cause,” he remarked.

He said that judgeship had given him “a great sense of satisfaction” by providing him with an opportunity to mitigate the sufferings of litigants and fulfil the constitutional promise of justice to citizens.
Recalling his early days as an advocate in Lucknow, Justice Upadhyaya said he had begun his legal career under the guidance of his father and other senior members of the Lucknow Bar.
